trust_boundaries: External to Internal: GitHub to ActionsRunner
Internal to Restricted: StagingEnv to ProdEnv
Internal to Restricted: DeployKey to ProdEnv
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted CI/CD pipeline with external source control and internal build/deploy infrastructure

threat_actors.name: External Supply Chain Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Compromise production systems via poisoned build artifacts or stolen credentials
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Malicious pull request or dependency injection into GitHub repository
non_capabilities: No physical access to data centers
No pre-existing valid accounts in the organization
No zero-day exploits for GitHub or Artifactory

threat_actors.name: Insider Threat
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration or sabotage of production systems
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Valid developer credentials with access to GitHub and CI/CD pipeline
non_capabilities: No ability to bypass hardware security modules
No access to production database backups
No ability to modify immutable audit logs

attack_paths.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious code committed to a public or private repository
attack_paths.impact: Execution of malicious code in CI/CD pipeline, leading to compromised artifacts
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Open-source dependencies and public repositories are frequent targets for supply chain attacks

attack_paths.entry_point: Exfiltration of secrets from CI/CD environment variables or configuration files
attack_paths.impact: Compromise of production credentials, allowing unauthorized access to production systems
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Secrets are often stored in environment variables or configuration files that may be exposed in logs or error messages

attack_paths.entry_point: Use of compromised developer credentials to trigger malicious CI/CD workflows
attack_paths.impact: Execution of arbitrary code in the CI/CD pipeline, leading to lateral movement and data exfiltration
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Developers often have broad access to CI/CD systems, and credential theft is a common initial access vector

attack_paths.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_paths.entry_point: Upload of malicious artifacts to the artifact registry
attack_paths.impact: Deployment of compromised software to staging and production environments
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Artifact registries are trusted sources for deployment, and malicious artifacts can bypass security checks

attack_paths.entry_point: Use of compromised deploy keys to access production systems
attack_paths.impact: Full compromise of production systems, including data exfiltration and service disruption
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Deploy keys are often stored in insecure locations and may be reused across environments

attack_paths.entry_point: Exfiltration of sensitive data from CI/CD environment to external servers
attack_paths.impact: Loss of confidential data, including source code, secrets, and customer data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: CI/CD environments often have outbound network access, making data exfiltration feasible

mitigations.control_name: Software and services are procured and maintained to incorporate appropriate security features
Access to local and remote systems is managed
Ensure that all software is signed and verified
Monitor and alert on anomalous outbound network activity

findings.severity_rationale: Supply chain compromise can lead to widespread deployment of malicious code
Exfiltration of secrets can lead to compromise of production systems
Use of valid accounts can lead to unauthorized access to CI/CD systems
Malicious artifacts in the registry can lead to deployment of compromised software
Compromise of deploy keys can lead to full compromise of production systems
Data exfiltration from CI/CD environment can lead to loss of confidential data
